Rashi on Yevamot 49a:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג: ורבי יהושע לכתוב רחמנא לא יגלה - כלומר, אי בשומרת יבם של אביו משתעי, או באנוסת אביו משתעי, לכתוב "לא יגלה כנף אביו" לחודיה, ולאשמעינן דיש ממזר מחייבי כריתות לרבנן, או מחייבי לאוין לרבי יהודה, וכל שכן מאשת אב, דהויא בכרת ומיתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:10:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: And Rabbi Yehoshua — let the Merciful One write "he shall not uncover" - That is to say, if [the verse] is speaking of his father's shomeret yavam [a widow awaiting levirate marriage], or speaking of a woman violated by his father, let it write "he shall not uncover his father's cloak" alone, and teach us that a mamzer [results] from [relations with] those liable to karet according to the Rabbis, or from those liable to negative commandments according to Rabbi Yehuda, and all the more so from one's father's wife, which involves karet and [judicial] death.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:10:2.hebrew: לא יקח - איש את אשת אביו, למה לי למכתב? אלא ש"מ מדכתביה, הא קמ"ל, דלא יבא ממזר עלה קאי, דמינה הוא דהוי ממזר משום דחייבי מיתות הוא, ואלא יגלה כנף אביו לא קאי. ואי קשיא: כנף אביו למאי כתביה? אי בשומרת יבם — לעבור עליו בשני לאוין: ערות אחי אביך לא תגלה, ולאו דלא יגלה כנף אביו; ואי באנוסת אביו — אשמעינן דאסורה:
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:10:2.english: Shall not take - [a man] his father’s wife — why do I need [Scripture] to write [this]? Rather, conclude from it that since [Scripture] wrote it, this is what it teaches us: that “[a] mamzer shall not enter” refers to her, for it is from her that [the offspring] is a mamzer because she is [among those] liable to death [penalties], whereas it does not refer to “and shall not uncover his father’s cloak.” And if you ask: For what [purpose] did [Scripture] write “his father’s cloak”? If [it refers] to [a woman] awaiting levirate marriage [with his father], [it is] to render him liable for two negative commandments: “the nakedness of your father’s brother you shall not uncover” and the negative commandment of “he shall not uncover his father’s cloak”; and if [it refers] to a woman violated by his father, it teaches us that she is forbidden.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:10:3.english: From "he shall not take" until "he shall not uncover" - That is, a father's wife, who is written between "he shall not take" and "he shall not uncover".

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:11:1.english: All agree - And even Shimon HaTeimani.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:11:2.hebrew: בבא על הנדה - אע"ג דקאי בכרת, אין הולד ממזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:11:2.english: One who engages in sexual relations with a menstruating woman - Even though he is subject to karet [excision], the child is not a mamzer.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:1:1.hebrew: כל שאר בשר שהוא בלא יבא - כל קורבה שהיא בלאו, ואפי' אין בה כרת; כגון אנוסת אביו, וכרבי יהודה, דהויא בלאו ד״לא יגלה כנף אביו״. ומחמת קורבה — כגון נושא חלוצתו, דהוי ב״לא יבנה״, והוי לאו דקורבה בלא כרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:1:1.english: Any next of kin that is [subject to] "he shall not enter" - Any kinship [that is prohibited] by a negative commandment, even if it does not carry [the penalty of] karet — such as [marrying] his father's rape victim, in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, as she is [prohibited] by the negative commandment of "he shall not uncover his father's skirt"; and [also a prohibition] due to kinship, such as one who marries his chalutzah, which is [prohibited] by "he shall not build," and is a negative commandment of kinship without karet.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:1:2.english: Any [relation] for which one is liable to karet - But [the child of] one who marries his chalutzah is not a mamzer.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:2:1.english: From a married woman - [That is,] those liable to capital punishment, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:2:2.hebrew: לקיים דברי רבי יהושע - לא היה כתוב במגלה, אלא ארישא קאי: אמר ר"ש בן עזאי לקיים דברי ר' יהושע כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:2:2.english: To confirm the words of Rabbi Yehoshua - [This] was not written in the scroll; rather, it refers back to the beginning [of the statement]: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said [this] to confirm the words of Rabbi Yehoshua, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:5:1.hebrew: דר' יהודה ורבנן - בפרק נושאין על האנוסה (לקמן יבמות דף צז.):
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:5:1.english: [The dispute] of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis - [It is] in the chapter [entitled] Nos'in al Ha'anusah (later, Yevamot 97a).

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:6:1.english: And it is written, "A mamzer shall not enter" - And adjacent to it [is written], "he shall not uncover [his father's garment]."

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:7:1.hebrew: ולרבי סימאי - בכתובות (דף כט:) וקידושין (דף סח.): מן הכל היה עושה ר"ע ממזרים, חוץ מאלמנה לכ"ג, שעושה חללין ולא ממזרי'. מדקאמר חוץ מאלמנה, אלמא אפי' חייבי לאוין שלא מחמת קורבה מרבה; כגון מחזיר גרושתו משנישאת, וכגן נתינה לישראל, דקיימא ב"לא תתחתן בם" (דברים ז׳:ג׳) — ומשבעה אומות הוא — וכגון עמוני שנשא בת ישראל, בניו ממזרים:
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:7:1.english: And according to Rabbi Simai - In Ketubot (29b) and Kiddushin (68a) [it is taught]: Rabbi Akiva would make mamzerim from all [forbidden unions], except for a widow [married] to a High Priest, where he makes chalalim and not mamzerim. Since he says "except for a widow," apparently he includes even [relations] liable for negative commandments that are not due to kinship — such as one who remarries his divorced wife after she had married [another], and such as a netinah [married] to an Israelite, who stands under [the prohibition of] "you shall not intermarry with them" (Deuteronomy 7:3) — [as] she is from the seven nations — and such as an Ammonite who married an Israelite woman — [that] his children are mamzerim.

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:7:2.hebrew: חייבי עשה - מצרי או אדומי קודם ג' דורות, דכתיב (דברים כ״ג:ט׳) דור שלישי יבא להם — ולא שני, ולאו הבא מכלל עשה, עשה. והא דר' ישבב נמי בכתובות (שם): בואו ונצוח על עקיבא בן יוסף, שהיה אומר כל שאין לו ביאה בישראל — הולד ממזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:7:2.english: Those liable for [violating] a positive commandment - An Egyptian or an Edomite before three generations, as it is written (Deuteronomy 23:9), "A third generation shall enter into them" — and not a second [generation], and a prohibition derived by implication from a positive commandment is [treated as] a positive commandment. And this [statement] of Rabbi Yeshevav is also [cited] in Ketubot (ibid.): "Come and let us cry out against Akiva ben Yosef, who used to say: anyone who does not have [permitted] marital relations among Israel, the offspring is a mamzer."

Rashi on Yevamot 49a:9:1.hebrew: סבר לה כרבנן - דפליגי אדרבי יהודה בנושאין על האנוסה (לקמן יבמות דף צז.), ואמרי: האי "לא יגלה כנף אביו" בשומרת יבם של אביו הכתוב מדבר, דהויא ליה אשת אחי אביו ובכרת. והאי דהדר כתבה במשנה תורה — משום למסמך ליה "לא יבא ממזר", ולאשמעינן דיש ממזר מחייבי כריתות:
Rashi on Yevamot 49a:9:1.english: He holds in accordance with the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda in [the chapter] Nos'in Al HaAnusah (below, Yevamot 97a), and say: [Regarding] this [verse], "He shall not uncover his father's garment" [Deuteronomy 23:1], the verse is speaking of a widow waiting for his father [to perform] levirate marriage, for she is his father's brother's wife, and [relations with her are punishable] by karet. And the reason [Scripture] wrote it again in Deuteronomy is in order to juxtapose "A mamzer shall not enter" [Deuteronomy 23:3] to it, and to teach us that a mamzer is [born] from [unions] liable to karet.

Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:10:1.hebrew: לכתוב רחמנא או לא יקח או לא יגלה - בקונטרס גרס: לכתוב רחמנא לא יגלה, ופי' דמלא יגלה לחודיה שמעינן דיש ממזר מחייבי כריתות לרבנן או מחייבי לאוין לר' יהודה; לא יקח איש את אשת אביו למה לי למכתב? אלא ש"מ מדכתביה דלא יבא ממזר עליה קאי, דמיניה הוא דהוי ממזר משום דחייבי מיתות ב"ד הוא, אבל אלא יגלה לא קאי, ובין לא יקח עד לא יגלה היינו אשת אב הכתובה בין לא יקח ללא יגלה. וקשה: חדא, שמוחק הספרים; ועוד, דבין לא יקח עד לא יגלה לא משמע כפירושו דקאי על אשת אב הכתובה בינתים; ועוד, אמאי כתב לא יגלה גבי ממזרות? ועוד, בחייבי מיתות דקילי כמו אשת איש, מנ"ל דהוי ממזר? ועוד, דליליף ר' יהושע שאר חייבי כריתות מהיקישא דר' יונה! ונראה לר"י כגירסת הספרים דגרסי: לכתוב רחמנא או לא יקח או לא יגלה, דמלא יקח נמי שמעינן כריתות, דהא דומיא דאשת אב דלא תפסי בה קידושין — דהא בהא תליא, כדפיר' לעיל (יבמות ד' מד: ד"ה עשאה), או מהיקישא דרבי יונה אתו, דאיתקיש כל העריות, כדאמרי' בריש הבא על יבמתו (לקמן יבמות ד' נד:). ומדכתב תרוייהו, ש"מ דמלא יקח, היינו חייבי סקילה, עד לא יגלה, דהיינו חייבי כריתות — הוי ממזר, ואתא לרבויי כל חייבי כריתות ומיתות קלות; וסבר כרבנן דבשומרת יבם הכתוב מדבר, ולא הוי לא יגלה בכלל, דאי הוי בכלל לא לכתוב אלא לא יגלה. ושמעון התימני נמי ה"מ למימר דסבר כר' יהודה דאמר באנוסת אביו הכתוב מדבר, ומלא יקח עד לא יגלה הוי הולד ממזר ואין לא יגלה בכלל, אלא דניחא ליה למימר דסבר כרבנן. ולפירוש ר"י, צ"ל לתנא דפירקין קמא דסבר כרבי יהודה דאמר באנוסת אביו הכתוב מדבר, וסבר נמי דאין ממזר מחייבי לאוין, דמלא יקח עד לא יגלה הוי ממזר ואין לא יגלה בכלל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:10:1.english: Let the Merciful One write either "he shall not take" or "he shall not uncover." - In the Kuntres [i.e., Rashi], [the text] reads: "Let the Merciful One write 'he shall not uncover,'" and he explained that from "he shall not uncover" alone we learn that there is a mamzer from [unions] liable to karet according to the Rabbis, or from [unions] liable to a negative prohibition according to Rabbi Yehudah; [so] why do I need [the Torah] to write "A man shall not take his father's wife"? Rather, learn from this—since it wrote it—that "a mamzer shall not enter" refers to it [i.e., his father's wife], that from it [i.e., that union] there is a mamzer because it is [a union] liable to court-imposed execution, whereas it does not refer to "he shall not uncover." And "between 'he shall not take' until 'he shall not uncover'" means [the prohibition of] a father's wife, which is written between "he shall not take" and "he shall not uncover." And this is difficult: First, that he erases [the reading of] the texts; furthermore, "between 'he shall not take' until 'he shall not uncover'" does not sound according to his explanation, that it refers to a father's wife which is written in between; furthermore, why did it write "he shall not uncover" regarding mamzerut? Furthermore, in [the case of unions] liable to lighter [forms of] execution, such as a married woman, from where do we know that [the offspring] is a mamzer? Furthermore, let Rabbi Yehoshua derive the rest of [the unions] liable to karet from the hekkesh [scriptural juxtaposition] of Rabbi Yonah! And it appears to the Ri [Rabbi Yitzchak] like the reading of the texts that read: "Let the Merciful One write either 'he shall not take' or 'he shall not uncover.'" For from "he shall not take" we also learn [unions liable to] karet, since it is similar to a father's wife, in that betrothal does not take effect with her—for one depends on the other, as we explained above (Yevamot 44b, s.v. Asa'ah)—or they come from the hekkesh of Rabbi Yonah, for all forbidden relations are juxtaposed to one another, as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] HaBa Al Yevimto (below, Yevamot 54b). And since it wrote both of them, learn from this that from "he shall not take"—which is [unions] liable to stoning—until "he shall not uncover"—which is [unions] liable to karet—[the offspring] is a mamzer, and it comes to include all [unions] liable to karet and lighter [forms of] execution; and he [Rabbi Yehoshua] holds like the Rabbis, that the verse speaks of a woman awaiting the yavam, and "he shall not uncover" is not included, for if it were included, it should only have written "he shall not uncover." And Shimon HaTimni could also have said that he holds like Rabbi Yehudah, who says the verse speaks of a woman violated by his father, and from "he shall not take" until "he shall not uncover" the child is a mamzer, while "he shall not uncover" is not included—except that it was preferable for him to say that he holds like the Rabbis. And according to the Ri's explanation, one must say regarding the Tanna of our first chapter, who holds like Rabbi Yehudah who says the verse speaks of a woman violated by his father, and also holds that there is no mamzer from [unions] liable to a negative prohibition, that from "he shall not take" until "he shall not uncover" [the offspring] is a mamzer, while "he shall not uncover" is not included.

Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:1:1.hebrew: שמעון התימני אומר כו' והלכה כדבריו - אע"ג דאין למדין הלכה מפי גמרא, הכא הלכתא כוותיה, דסתמא דפרק האומר (קדושין דף סו: ושם) נראה עיקר, דכהאי גוונא קרי הלכתא פסיקתא בבבא קמא (ד' קב.) ובמסכת ע"ז (דף ז: ושם) בההיא דכל המשנה ידו על התחתונה. ולעיל בפ' קמא (יבמות דף יד. ושם) אמר: פשיטא, בני חייבי לאוין כשרים נינהו. ובפרק שני (לעיל יבמות כג.) קאמר רב פפא: מסתברא חייבי לאוין תפסי בהו קידושין. ולעיל (יבמות דף מה.) פסקינן דעובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל — הולד כשר. וכמה אמוראי דאיירי בצרת מחזיר גרושתו, ולר"ע לא משכחת לה צרה דאין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין. וכרבי יהושע נמי יש להוכיח דלא קי"ל כוותיה, דאמר לעיל (שם:): ושניהם לא למדוה אלא מאשת אב, וחייבי כריתות דמו לאשת אב לכולי עלמא. ולעיל בריש פירקין (יבמות דף לז.) קאמר ראב"י דהלכתא כוותיה דאין ממזר מספק, משמע דהויא ממזר מאשת אח. ולעיל (יבמות ד' מ:) אמר רב טובי בר קיסנא: הבא על צרת חלוצתו — הולד ממזר, ואפילו רבי יוחנן לא פליג אלא משום דצרה כחלוצה בלאו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:1:1.english: Shimon HaTimni says, etc., "and the halakha is in accordance with his statement." - Even though one does not derive halakha from a Gemara [statement], here the halakha is in accordance with him, for the anonymous Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer (Kiddushin 66b and there) appears to be the primary [ruling], as [the Gemara] calls such a case "settled halakha" (hilkheta pesikta) in Bava Kamma (102a) and in Tractate Avodah Zarah (7b and there) regarding [the rule of] "whoever alters [the terms] has the lower hand." And earlier in the first chapter (Yevamot 14a and there) [the Gemara] says: "It is obvious that the children of [unions prohibited by] negative commandments are fit [and not mamzerim]." And in the second chapter (earlier, Yevamot 23a) Rav Pappa says: "It stands to reason that betrothal takes effect for [unions prohibited by] negative commandments." And earlier (Yevamot 45a) we rule that when a gentile or a slave engages in intercourse with a Jewish woman, the child is fit. And several Amoraim discuss the rival wife of one who remarries his divorcee, whereas according to Rabbi Akiva you cannot find a rival wife [in that case], since betrothal does not take effect for [unions prohibited by] negative commandments. And regarding Rabbi Yehoshua as well, it can be proven that we do not rule in accordance with him, for [the Gemara] says earlier (ibid. [45b]): "And both of them derived it only from a father's wife," and [unions] liable to karet are analogous to a father's wife according to everyone. And earlier at the beginning of our chapter (Yevamot 37a) [the Gemara] says [that] Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov['s view] is the halakha — that there is no mamzer out of doubt — which implies that [a child] from a brother's wife is a mamzer. And earlier (Yevamot 40b) Rav Tovi bar Kisna says: "One who engages in intercourse with the rival wife of his chalutzah — the child is a mamzer," and even Rabbi Yochanan only disagrees because a rival wife is like a chalutzah [who is subject only to] a negative commandment.

Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:1:2.hebrew: רבי יהושע אומר כל שחייבין עליו כו' - יש מגיהים ר' יהודה במקום רבי יהושע, דבפרק עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף עד:) גבי "כל האסורין לבא בקהל מותרים לבא זה בזה ור' יהודה אוסר", ומפרש עלה דר' יהודה סבר דממזר מאחותו לא הוי ממזר אלא מאשת איש, ופריך עלה "תנינא" מהך דהכא. ואין נראה, דהיאך היה בן עזאי אומר לקיים מילתיה דר' יהודה, והא קשיש מיניה טובא? דהא בן עזאי תלמיד חבר הוה לרבי עקיבא, כדאמר במי שמת (ב"ב ד' קנח:), ור' יהודה מתלמידי בתראי דר' עקיבא הוה. ועוד, דר' יהודה סבר כרבי עקיבא דיש ממזר מחייבי לאוין, כדפרישית לעיל (יבמות ד' מז.) גבי ההוא דאתא לקמיה דרבי יהודה, וכדאמר בפ' ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין ד' נג: ושם). אלא ודאי ר' יהושע גרסינן; והתם פריך "תנינא" משום דהוה ליה למיתני "וכן היה רבי יהודה אומר כדבריו", אי הוה סבר כר' יהושע. ומיהו התם דפריך "תנינא", הוה מצי למיפרך טפי שפיר: דלא אפשר לומר דלר' יהודה ממזר מאחותו לא הוי ממזר, כיון דמוקי קרא באנוסת אביו, וסבר כר"ע דיש ממזר מחייבי לאוין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:1:2.english: "Rabbi Yehoshua says: Any [forbidden relation] for which one is liable, etc." - Some emend [the text to read] "Rabbi Yehudah" instead of "Rabbi Yehoshua", because in the chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 74b), regarding [the Mishnah]: "All those who are forbidden to enter the congregation are permitted to marry one another, and Rabbi Yehudah forbids [it]," [the Gemara] explains regarding it that Rabbi Yehudah holds that a [child] from one's sister is not a mamzer, rather only [one] from a married woman, and [the Gemara] asks against it: "We [already] learned this!" from this [Mishnah] here. But this does not seem [correct], for how could Ben Azzai say [his statement] to confirm the words of Rabbi Yehudah, when he [Ben Azzai] was much older than him [Rabbi Yehudah]? For Ben Azzai was a student-colleague of Rabbi Akiva, as it says in [the chapter] Mi SheMeit (Bava Batra 158b), whereas Rabbi Yehudah was among the later students of Rabbi Akiva. And furthermore, Rabbi Yehudah holds like Rabbi Akiva that a mamzer is produced from [unions] liable to negative commandments, as I explained above (Yevamot 47a) regarding that [man] who came before Rabbi Yehudah, and as it says in the chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 53b, and there). Rather, we certainly read "Rabbi Yehoshua" [in our Mishnah]; and there [in Kiddushin], [the Gemara] asks "We [already] learned this!" because [the Tanna] should have taught: "And so too Rabbi Yehudah would say in accordance with his words," if he [Rabbi Yehudah] held like Rabbi Yehoshua. However, there where [the Gemara] asks "We [already] learned this!", it could have asked an even better [objection]: that it is impossible to say that according to Rabbi Yehudah [a child] from one's sister is not a mamzer, since he establishes the verse as referring to a woman raped by one's father, and he holds like Rabbi Akiva that a mamzer is produced from [unions] liable to negative commandments.

Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:2:1.hebrew: איש פלוני ממזר מאשת איש כו' - תימה, דלא נקט חייבי מיתות ב"ד סתם; ואי משום דמעשה שהיה כך היה, א"כ מנ"ל דהוי כר' יהושע? וי"ל דנקט אשת איש לרבותא, דאע"פ שהוא קל משאר חייבי מיתות — דהוי בחנק, ויש לה היתר בחיי אוסרה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:2:1.english: "So-and-so is a mamzer from a married woman," etc. - [This is] puzzling, for it did not state "those liable to court-imposed capital punishment" in general. And if [it was] because the incident that occurred was thus, if so, how do we know that [the law] is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua? And one can answer that it stated "a married woman" to teach a novelty: that even though it is more lenient than other [prohibitions carrying] capital punishment — for it is [punishable] by strangulation, and she has [a means of] permissibility during the lifetime of the one who forbids her [i.e., her husband, through divorce] — [nevertheless, the child is a mamzer].

Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:4:1.hebrew: וכתיב לא יבא ממזר - וא"ת: והא מפסיק קרא ד"לא יבא פצוע דכא" בינתים? וי"ל: דכיון דלאו בני בנים נינהו, ולא שייך מינייהו ממזר, לא חשיב הפסק:
Tosafot on Yevamot 49a:4:1.english: And it is written: "A mamzer shall not enter" - And if you ask: Does not the verse "One with crushed testicles shall not enter" [Deuteronomy 23:2] intervene between them? One can answer: Since they are incapable of having children, and [the status of] mamzer does not apply to them, it is not considered an interruption.
